questions.question: What transmission fluid and lubricant-change practices are recommended for prolonged operation below -15°F (-26°C)?
What transmission fluid maintenance and fluid types are recommended for prolonged operation below -15°F (-26°C)?
What transmission fluid and lubricant-change practices are recommended for prolonged operation below -15°F (-26°C)?

claims.text: For prolonged operation below -15°F (-26°C), the general lubricant-change instruction is to change the transmission fluid more frequently.
Increased viscosity and potential fluid degradation at low temperatures are the stated reasons for changing the transmission fluid more frequently.
The transmission PMCS notes specify a synthetic transmission fluid suitable for arctic conditions, such as MIL-PRF-83133 or a high-performance synthetic fluid approved for use in cold environments.

TM 9-2320-280-20-1 (1996, including Change 2 dated 2004) recommends Type 1 or Type 2 synthetic fluids for arctic conditions, depending on the transmission model, to ensure proper lubrication and performance in extreme cold.
